memos.headline: Hyatt beat Q3 EPS by 65% and raised its 2026 RevPAR outlook; revenue narrowly missed
reasoning: Source: Hyatt's Q3 release, figures on Benzinga Newsdesk at 07:05 ET: 'Q3 Adj. EPS $1.27 Beats $0.77 Estimate, Sales $1.743B Miss $1.747B Estimate'. Benzinga's 08:28 summary: comparable system-wide RevPAR '+7.2% year over year, led by luxury properties'; gross fees '+15.2% to $327 million'; full-year RevPAR growth forecast raised.
What changed: fee income and RevPAR are running well ahead of plan. Revenue is down 2.4% y/y only because of hotels sold in 2025 (an asset-light shift); adjusted EBITDA is +19% excluding them.
Timing: before the open; no session has traded it. Pre-market: Benzinga says the stock 'rose premarket'; IEX shows no prints against the 173.32 close.
objections: Benzinga reports a pre-market rise we cannot see on IEX; part of the beat may already be priced.

memos.headline: The EPS beat is mostly one-offs and fees from a year of asset sales; no mispricing I can size
reasoning: What changed: adjusted EPS of $1.27 against $0.77 is a 65% beat, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 6.2% ($295M), or 19% excluding sold hotels. A 65% EPS beat on 6% EBITDA growth points to below-the-line items (tax, interest, gains) rather than operations, and the summary does not break them out.

Operations: RevPAR +7.2% and fees +15.2% are good, and the full-year RevPAR raise confirms them. But the summary gives no size for the raise and no full-year EPS or EBITDA guide to compare with consensus.
Price: Benzinga says the stock rose pre-market, size unknown. With the operating beat moderate and the headline beat inflated, the open is likely to price what is real.
Would prove this wrong: H up more than 5% by Monday's close.
objections: Headline EPS beat not matched by EBITDA; no full-year guide figures.
